sentences.text:
The facts leading to the filing of the present petition are that the notification dated 29.06.2009 under Section 4 of the L.A. Act, 1894 was issued by the Land Acquisition Collector (hereinafter referred to as "LAC") for acquisition of land/properties for the purpose of widening of road at G.T.
Road, Near Apsara Border Delhi situated in Village Jhilmil Tahirpur, which was followed by the Notification dated 13.07.2009 under Section 6 & 17 of L.A. Act, 1894.

The LAC has mentioned in the award that the Delhi Development Authority was asked to clarify the land use of the land under acquisition and the DDA vide a reply dated 28.02.2011 stated that the properties were partly industrial and partly commercial [District Centre] as per the Zonal Development Plan of Zone-E.
Furthermore, the LAC has mentioned in his award that on further clarification from the DDA with respect to which part of land was Industrial and which part of land was commercial [District Centre], the DDA provided the survey plan of the District Centre, Dilshad Garden of the year 1996-97 which indicated that the khasra numbers which were acquired vide the present award fell in the District Centre Dilshad Garden.

The LAC, by giving a list of various registered lease agreements and sale deeds of the area, assessed the market value of the area on the basis of Industrial circle rates notified by the Govt. of NCT of Delhi on 18.07.2007 vide notification no.F.2[12]/Fin(E-I)/Part file/Vol.-I(ii)/3548 dated 18.07.2007 of the Category 'G' of the said circle rates.
A total area of 1012.50 sq. mtrs. was acquired vide above award.

Further solatium at the rate of 30% of market value alongwith the additional amount @ 12% of market value w.e.f. 29.06.2009 to 20.10.2009 [date of possession] was allowed apart from cost of structure appended to the said land and statutory interest under Section 34 of Act.
Thus, an Award for total amount of Rs.4,51,44,028.00 was passed by the LAC.
4 Being aggrieved from the lesser rate fiXed by LAC for the acquired land, the petitioners filed a petition under Section 18 of L.A. Act, 1894 before the LAC.

The LAC sent the present reference petition to this court for adjudication and subsequently the present case was listed for trial and finally the present matter has come before this Court for final adjudication.

5 In the present petition, the petitioners filed their reference petition U/s 18 of the LA Act and have raised various grounds inter alia stating that the market value assessed by Ld. LAC is not proper and is on a much lower side than the prevailing market value of the area.

The petitioners further contended that admittedly the land use of the acquired property bearing No.485- A/1 & 485-A/2,
corresponding to Khasra No. 1183/220 [New] situated on the Main GT Road, Jhilmil-Tahirpur,
Delhi was commercial and the petitioners were using the acquired property for commercial purposes i.e. Sale & Purchase of Cars under the name & style of M/s Raghuvanshi Motors Pvt. Ltd.,
much prior to the date of notification U/s 4 of the Act.
The petitioners further contended that they were the absolute owners of the plot in question.

The petitioners have further contended that the Smt. Meena W/O Sh. Sham Sunder vs Union Of India on 5 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2295989/
2 LAC has not appreciated the cogent evidence given by them at the time of passing of the award.

sentences.text: The petitioners further contended that their land was commercial as per the Zonal development plan of Zone 'E' and in spite of the said admission, the LAC failed to assess commercial market rates to the acquired property of the petitioners which was situated on the Main GT Road.

6 The petitioners have further contended that the land of the petitioners was freehold land which was much higher than the leasehold properties and that even the Govt. of India levied certain charges in the form of percentage while converting leasehold to freehold.

It is submitted that LAC failed to appreciate that the land was commercial and all the amenities for running industrial/commercial sites were available much prior to the date of notification U/s 4 of the Act.
The petitioners further stated that the market value of the land was not less than Rs.2,00,000/- per sq. mtr. as on the date of notification U/s 4 of LA Act.
7 Notice of reference petition was issued to both respondents.

The respondent no.1 has contested the reference petition by filing written statement thereby taking various preliminary objections that the compensation assessed by the LAC is sufficient and reasonable and it reflects the true market value prevailing at the time of the notification under Section 4 of the LA Act and that various other facts were taken into account while assessing the market value.
The petitioner is claiming excessive and exorbitant market value of the land and structures.
The LAC in order to assess the fair market value of the land considered the "Schedule of Market Rates" of lands in Delhi.
The claim of the owners/interested persons were duly considered and since the same is without any merit or any documentary evidence the same was rightly rejected by the LAC.
The petition is barred by limitation.
On merits, all averments/grounds of claim petition were denied word by word and ultimately it is prayed that the present petition is devoid of any merits and be dismissed.

8 Respondent no.2 adopted the written statement filed by respondent no.2.
9

After completion of pleadings following issues were framed by my Ld. Predecessor vide order dated 28.05.2014:-
1
Whether the claimant proves that the compensation arrived at by the Land Acquisition Officer is unfair in the circumstances of the given case and calls for enhancement?

2 Relief.
10

The petitioners proved the schedule of commercial L&DO rates for the relevant period issued by the Ministry of Urban affairs, Govt. of India as Ex.PW5/1.
The petitioners further proved the zonal development plan of Zone-E in which the acquired area was shown as commercial.
The said evidence was exhibited as Ex.PW-9/1 & PW-9/2.
The petitioners also proved the master plan which was exhibited as Ex.PW-10/1 to PW-10/3.

Apart from the said evidence, the petitioners also proved one registered sale deed of the locality and summoned the record of an award passed by the LAC Distt. West bearing No.4/DC/W/2010-11 as Ex. PW-6/1.

The petitioners proved the said award in order to claim Smt. Meena W/O Sh. Sham Sunder vs Union Of India on 5 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2295989/

The said witness came and proved the award and exhibited the attested copy of the same.
During cross examination, he deposed that he did not have any personal knowledge of the record brought by him.

12 On the other hand, the ld. Counsel for the respondent no.1 had tendered in evidence the copy of award No.1/11-12 as Ex.R-1 passed by the LAC in which the market value of the acquired property was fixed at Rs.27,400/- per sq. mtr. which was on the basis of Industrial circle rates announced on 18.07.2007. 13

By exhibiting the copy of the award Ex.R-1, the respondent no.1 duly admitted the location and potentiality of the acquired properties to be commercial in nature since the LAC has himself stated that as per the letter dated 28.02.2011 submitted by the Delhi Development Authority, the acquired khasra numbers fell in the Distt. Centre Dilshad Garden which would go in a long way for determining the actual market value of the acquired properties as on the date of notification U/s 4 of the Act.
The respondent no.1 did not give any other evidence and thereafter the evidence of the respondent no.1 was closed.

The respondent no.2 chose not to lead any evidence at all and adopted the evidence filed by respondent no.1 and therefore all the evidence led by the petitioner was unrebutted by either of the respondents.
14 Ld. counsel for petitioner filed written arguments and she submitted that she does not want to submit anything else beyond written arguments.

On the other hand, ld. counsel for respondent no.1 did not file written arguments and he adopted the written arguments as filed by him in case titled as 'Jaspal Singh Manchanda Vs Union of India' & Ganesh Cold Storage Vs Union of India, bearing LAC no.13/16 and LAC no.16/16 respectively.

16 I have also perused the record.

My issue wise finding is as under:
ISSUE NO.1 17 Onus to prove this issue was upon the petitioners and they were required to prove that the compensation arrived at by the Land Acquisition Officer is unfair in the circumstances of the given case and calls for enhancement.

First and foremost, for the ascertainment of the actual market value, it is necessary to consider the admissions made by all the parties in the pleadings as well as in their evidence led in support of their contentions.
The relevant portion of the award announced by the LAC is reproduced herein-under:-
"The Delhi Development Authority was asked to clarify the status of land under acquisition as per Master / Zonal Development Plan.

The DDA in its reply dated 28.02.2011 stated that the land use of the site under reference is partly industrial and partly commercial [District Centre] as per Zonal development plan of Zone-E.
Thereafter the DDA was further asked to clarify the part of land which is of industrial Smt. Meena W/O Sh. Sham Sunder vs Union Of India on 5 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2295989/
4 use and the part of land which is of commercial use [District Centre] as per Zonal development plan.

sentences.text: In response, the DDA provided survey plan of Distt. Centre Dilshad Garden [near 'I' pocket] of the year 1996-97, which indicates the Khasra Number falls within Distt. Centre Dilshad Garden.
These khasra numbers are claimed by the interested persons as commercial land/plot at S.No.14 & 15 under the heading "Claims and Evidence".
18 The LAC has assessed the market value on the basis of certain registered sale deeds of the acquired area which were Industrial in nature.

Out of the 14 sale deeds mentioned in the award,
three sale deeds were allegedly pertaining to commercial properties and the rest of sale deeds were in respect of Industrial properties.
However the land value per sq. mtr. in respect of all the properties was arrived at Rs.27,400/- per sq. mtr. which was the rate for Industrial category of circle rates of Category-G.

A perusal of the 14 sale deeds mentioned in the award clearly revealed that there was no difference in the market value per sq. mtr. with respect to the sale of industrial as well as commercial properties and therefore no importance could be attached to the said sale deeds.
Even the respondents did not prove the sale deeds in any manner and therefore they cannot be taken into consideration by this court for determination of market value.

It cannot be determined in any manner whether the said sale deeds were executed between a willing seller and a willing purchaser which is one of the most important aspects for determination of market value on the basis of sale deeds.
19 The onus to prove the market value was upon the petitioners.

As per section 23 of the Land Acquisition Act, the market value of the acquired properties is liable to be ascertained / determined as on the date of issuance of notification U/s 4 of the LA Act which in this particular case is 29.06.2009.
The petitioner has duly stated that the rate of Rs.27,400/- per sq. mtr. as assessed by the LAC is extremely meagre for the prime commercial property of the petitioner.

20 During the course of the proceedings in the present matter, this court has already determined the market value with respect to the properties situated in the same Revenue Estate i.e. Jhilmil Tahirpur Delhi which have been acquired vide award Nos.2/07-08 wherein the date of notification U/s 4 of the LA Act was 12.04.2006 and award No.1/08-09 wherein the date of notification U/s 4 of the LA Act was 14.10.2005.

The location and potentiality of all the properties acquired vide the present award and the properties acquired vide award No.2/07-08 and 1/08-09 are identical since they are all situated on GT Road in Jhilmil Tahirpur Delhi.

It is ironical that in award No.2/07-08 pertaining to the same area i.e. Jhilmil Tahirpur, the LAC has based the said award on the basis of schedule of market rates considering the acquired properties to be commercial in nature, however in this very award which was passed almost three years subsequently, he has stated that though the khasra numbers acquired are commercial however, industrial circle rates of the year 2007 are applicable to the acquired properties.

21 Section 23 of L.A. Act, 1894 provides that in order to determine the amount of compensation to be awarded for land acquired under this Act, the Court shall take into consideration the market value of the land on the date of publication of notification under section 4 (1).

UOI (MANU/SC/0947/2014), the Hon'ble Apex Court has observed that market value is ordinarily the price the property may fetch in the open market if sold by a willing seller unaffected by the special needs of a particular purchase, and where definite material is not forthcoming either in the shape of sales of similar lands in the neighborhood at or about the date of notification under Section 4 (1) or otherwise, other sale instances as well as other evidence have to be considered.

It has been further observed that for the purpose of fiXation of fair and reasonable market value of any type of land, abnormally high value or abnormally low value sales should be carefully discarded.

26 In the written arguments, the counsel for the petitioner has relied upon the judgment dated 25.02.2023 passed by this court in case titled Chandra Pratap Singh Vs. UOI bearing LAC No.27/2020 which was passed on the basis of the market value arrived in properties acquired vide award no.2/07-08.

sentences.text: In the said judgment, this court has enhanced the market value of the properties acquired from Rs.6450/- per sq. mtr. to Rs.48,000/- per sq. mtr. wherein the date of notification U/s 4 of the LA Act was 12.04.2006.

After considering the facts and circumstances of the present case, the evidence filed on record and the judgment delivered with respect to the properties acquired vide award No.2/07-08 and 1/08-09, Jhilmil Tahirpur Delhi, I am also inclined to enhance the market value after giving an appreciation of 10% per annum from the date of notification U/s 4 of the LA Act of award no.2/07-08 i.e.
12.04.2006 till the date of notification U/s 4 of the LA Act in the present case i.e.
29.06.2009.

27 Ld. counsel for the petitioners has also brought to the notice of this Court that some of the khasra numbers which have been acquired vide the present award and award Nos.2/07-08 and 1/08- 09 are same and are therefore bound to be similar in location, potentiality and market value.

28 A perusal of the award bearing No.2/07-08 pertaining to Village Jhilmil Tahirpur itself shows that part khasra numbers have been acquired vide the said award for the purpose of MRTS project and part of the same khasra number has been subsequently acquired vide the present award for the purpose of widening of GT Road at Apsara Border.
29 The LAC has himself admitted in both the awards that the land use of both the properties is commercial.

Ld. counsel for the petitioners has relied upon various judgments in support of her contentions and specifically relied upon a judgment passed by this court itself titled as Monika Gupta Vs. Union of India & Anr.
bearing LAC No.7/20 which is in respect of the properties acquired vide award No.2/07-08 and in view of the earlier discussion, I hereby determine the market value of the properties acquired vide the present award to be Rs.62,500/- per sq. mtrs. as on the date of notification i.e. 29.06.2009 being approximately three years & two months subsequent to the date of notification U/s 4 of LA Act of award No.2/07-08 Jhilmil Tahirpur Delhi.

The sale deeds relied upon by the collector do not give any reason for me to hold that they were genuine or bonafide in any manner.

31 Ld. counsel for petitioners has also relied upon the judgment passed in case titled Chandra Pratap Singh Vs. UOI bearing LAC No.27/2020 as well as the judgment in the award No.1/08-09 titled as GR Khan Vs. UOI bearing LAC No.73A/2011.

7 32
The LAC has awarded an amount of Rs.27,400/- per sq. mtr.
A perusal of the file also reveals that the petitioners has never received any amount over and above the awarded amount of compensation of Rs.27,400/- per sq. mtr.

Therefore, the petitioners are now entitled to the market value @
Rs.62,500 thereby giving an enhancement of Rs.35,100/- over and above the amount assessed by the LAC @ Rs.27,400/- per sq. mtr.
Accordingly the petitioner is entitled to a further enhancement of Rs.35,100/- per sq. mtr. over and above Rs.27,400/- per sq. mtr.
The petitioners would be entitled to the said enhancement on the area mentioned in the statement under section 19 of the LA Act.
RELIEF 33
In view of the findings of issue No.1 the petitioners are entitled to the market value @ Rs.62,500/- per sq. mtr. as on 29.06.2009.

In addition, the petitioners would also be entitled to all statutory benefits i.e. 30% solatium on the market value in view of the compulsory nature of acquisition U/s 23 (2) of the LA Act and an additional amount of 12% per annum on the market value from the date of notification U/s 4 of the LA Act till date of possession or award whichever is earlier as per section 23 (1A) of the LA Act.

Besides the petitioner would also be entitled to interest on the enhanced amount of compensation @ 9% per annum from the date of dispossession till expiry of one year and thereafter @ 15% per annum till the date of payment of the balance amount.
34 Reference is answered accordingly.
Parties to bear their own costs.
Decree sheet be prepared accordingly.
35 A copy of this judgement be sent to the concerned LAC for information and necessary compliance.
File be consigned to Record Room as per rules.

Rs.62,500 thereby giving an enhancement of Rs.35,100/- over and above the amount assessed by the LAC @ Rs.27,400/- per sq. mtr.
Accordingly the petitioner is entitled to a further enhancement of Rs.35,100/- per sq. mtr. over and above Rs.27,400/- per sq. mtr.
The petitioners would be entitled to the said enhancement on the area mentioned in the statement under section 19 of the LA Act.
RELIEF 33
In view of the findings of issue No.1 the petitioners are entitled to the market value @ Rs.62,500/- per sq. mtr. as on 29.06.2009.
In addition, the petitioners would also be entitled to all statutory benefits i.e. 30% solatium on the market value in view of the compulsory nature of acquisition U/s 23 (2) of the LA Act and an additional amount of 12% per annum on the market value from the date of notification U/s 4 of the LA Act till date of possession or award whichever is earlier as per section 23 (1A) of the LA Act.
Besides the petitioner would also be entitled to interest on the enhanced amount of compensation @ 9% per annum from the date of dispossession till expiry of one year and thereafter @ 15% per annum till the date of payment of the balance amount.
34 Reference is answered accordingly.
Parties to bear their own costs.
Decree sheet be prepared accordingly.
35 A copy of this judgement be sent to the concerned LAC for information and necessary compliance.
